pr_title: usb: device_next: hid: fix Get Report buffer handling
pr_body:
After the get_report() callback, we need to determine how many bytes the HID device wrote to the report buffer. Use the callback return value to do this, and modify the net_buf data length value if get_report was successful.

Fixes: #73457

issue_context.title: usb: device_next: usbd_hid: HID get report does not work
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
HID get report functionality does not work for USB next stack. `ioctl: Connection timed out` error is observed e.g. when host computer tries to get a HID feature report from device. Issue was replicated with an application developed outside of Zephyr, but the root cause is bug in the USB next stack.

**Expected behavior**
HID report get should work without problems.

**Impact**
A HID device using USB next stack cannot support HID report get.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
Issue affects main branch (`c1400536548bb861c630f81d8aced864f1a85ca1`).

**Additional context**
Seems that incrementing data length of the buffer can be a workaround here: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/73451.

review_comments: Should there be an assert here to check that `ret <= size`?
Not sure, maybe requesting data that is larger than a report length is fine from the host's perspective. The idea is to do our best not to fail here.

Host requesting more than report length is not what would be asserted here. When `ret <= size` is not fulfilled it means that application essentially wrote (or at least claimed to write) beyond the buffer.
